summary: Deployed and verified an "inventory application" on node1 (RHEL 7.9) served over TCP 8181 with SELinux in enforcing mode throughout, then completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery protocol.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1: RHEL 7.9, SELinux enforcing (SELINUXTYPE=targeted), no repos/subscription so no package installs possible (semanage/semodule/checkmodule/audit2allow all absent), no pre-existing inventory app.

Created /opt/inventory-app/index.html (inventory listing) and /opt/inventory-app/server.py (Python2 BaseHTTPServer/SimpleHTTPServer) bound to 0.0.0.0:8181; applied SELinux file contexts (bin_t on server.py, httpd_sys_content_t on index.html).
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory-app.service (ExecStart=/usr/bin/python2 /opt/inventory-app/server.py, Restart=on-failure, WantedBy=multi-user.target); started it via systemctl.
Opened TCP 8181 permanently in firewalld and reloaded.

Verified service runs in system_u:system_r:unconfined_service_t domain, listens on *:8181, and HTTP 200 responses returned via both 127.0.0.1 and $NODE_IP while `getenforce` reported Enforcing at every check; confirmed no AVC denials (dmesg/audit log empty/absent).

Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/SELinux baseline, issued a detached `sudo -n reboot` on node1, polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, confirmed boot_id changed (809708f3... -> 9ea46e0a...), and re-verified SELinux enforcing, service active+enabled, port listening, firewalld rule persisted, and HTTP 200 after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Baseline: SELinux enforcing and system state before changes
evidence.summary: Confirmed RHEL 7.9, SELINUX=enforcing, no package manager access, and absence of semanage/semodule tooling, establishing the constraint that the app must run in a domain compatible with enforcing SELinux without new port policy modules.

evidence.requirement: Inventory application served on TCP 8181 while SELinux stays enforcing
evidence.summary: Deployed inventory-app.service, confirmed getenforce=Enforcing before and after start, service active, listening on *:8181 as unconfined_service_t, firewalld port 8181/tcp opened, and curl to 127.0.0.1:8181 and $NODE_IP:8181 both returned HTTP 200 with inventory content; no AVC denials found.
Captured boot_id 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799, service enabled state, and Enforcing SELinux status prior to restarting node1.
Issued a detached sudo -n reboot that returned its acknowledgement before disconnecting; subsequent exec attempts timed out, confirming the node was mid-restart.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving the restart occurred
evidence.summary: boot_id read back as 9ea46e0a-ee13-4d39-806a-25b40765c05f, differing from the pre-restart 809708f3-... value, proving a genuine reboot rather than mere service restart.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and SELinux enforcement
evidence.summary: After reboot, getenforce still Enforcing, inventory-app.service active and enabled, listening on 8181 in unconfined_service_t, firewalld still has 8181/tcp open, and curl to $NODE_IP:8181 returned HTTP 200 with the inventory page.
